newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy to cut 1998 deficit by 24 trln lire - papers.
newsitem.headline: Italy to cut 1998 deficit by 24 trln lire - papers.

text.p: The Italian Treasury is looking at the prospect of a 1998 budget containing at least 24 trillion lire of deficit-cutting measures, newspapers said on Friday.
Corriere della Sera said the Treasury was considering a package of budgetary measures worth 25-30 trillion lire in a bid to tame the deficit for entry into European monetary union.

It said in an unsourced report that the deficit would be greater than 3.9 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) without the measures. The Maastricht treaty sets the target ceiling at three percent for single currency aspirants.
La Repubblica newspaper said Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi would need to draw up a package worth 24 trillion lire "or even something more".

Centre-left Prime Minister Romano Prodi has introduced nearly 100 trillion lire of belt-tightening measures since taking office a year ago in a bid to make Italy a founder member of economic and monetary union (EMU).

Earlier this week, Ciampi said Italy's public sector borrowing requirement in the first half of 1997 is expected to fall by more than 50 percent compared with the same period in 1996, when it reached 52.25 trillion lire.

Cabinet undersecretary Enrico Micheli, who has previously spoken of measures worth around 18 trillion lire, said on Thursday the budget would not be brought forward as had been proposed earlier this year to prove Italy's European credentials.
Ciampi, asked whether Italy would need to pass deficit curbing measures of 25 trillion lire, told reporters in Washington in April that it was too early to go into figures.
A senior economic aide of Prodi said late last month that budget cuts of at least 25 trillion lire would be needed if Italy was to qualify in the first wave of EMU.
